title: Arkis collateral haircuts are signed and two-sided, discounting short exposure as well as long
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.7.2.2.1.1 defines the Collateral Haircut as "the minimum discount applied to net exposure to an asset while calculating position health and stress tested portfolio value, expressed as a **negative percentage for accounts net long** an asset, or a **positive percentage for accounts net short** an asset." The live configuration shows the pairs directly: BTC and ETH at +20% / −20%, DOGE and ADA at +25% / −25%, ZEC and AVAX at +30% / −30%.

Conventional lending haircuts are one-directional because conventional lending only holds collateral long: value the asset below market, and a price fall is absorbed. A prime brokerage account can be net short, and a short position's risk is a price *rise* — unbounded, unlike a long's floor at zero.

Applying the haircut with a sign makes the stress test symmetric. A net-short SOL position is marked as though SOL rose 20%; a net-long one as though it fell 20%. The account must survive whichever direction hurts it, which is the only coherent way to margin a book that can face either way.

The signed formulation also composes correctly across a portfolio. Because the haircut attaches to *net* exposure per asset with a direction, a portfolio's stressed value can be computed by summing per-asset stresses rather than by enumerating scenarios.

The stablecoin rows show the framework's range: USDT and USDC at 0%, fully reserved USD stablecoins at −5%, Ethena USDe at −10% — all one-sided negatives, because a dollar stablecoin's realistic failure is breaking downward and there is no symmetric upside risk to price. The sign is not decoration; it encodes which direction each asset can actually surprise you in.
description: Each asset carries a negative percentage for net-long accounts and a positive one for net-short, so stress testing prices adverse moves in both directions instead of only downside.
